title: Before sleep
hookLine: in Your name I die and I live, before lying down (Bukhari)
last: IQAMAH — KNOCK AT THE OPEN DOOR.

lines: THE LAST THING: ONE MORE VIDEO.
A WEEK OF ASKING ENDS HERE.
cards: Here's the last thing most people do every day: scroll. Lights off, face lit blue, one more video, one more headline. Then the phone drops, and you're gone.
Seven or eight hours when you don't know where you are, can't guard anything, can't answer anyone. It's the most helpless you'll be all day, and it gets treated as nothing.
This whole week has been about asking: just ask, a heavy heart, he is near, good here and there, for the absent, at the open times. It ends at the edge of sleep. Today: before sleep.

teach.h: IN YOUR NAME I DIE AND I LIVE.
teach.b: Bukhari reports from the companion Hudhayfah that when the Prophet ﷺ lay down at night, he put his hand under his cheek and said: bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya. In Your name, O Allah, I die and I live.
It's very short, and striking: it calls sleep a kind of dying. That isn't just poetry.

The Qur'an, in Surah az-Zumar, says Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and also takes, in their sleep, the souls that have not died; He keeps the ones whose death is decreed and sends the others back until a set time.
Every night, in this picture, is a small rehearsal.
You let go of everything, and you're handed back in the morning. So the same hadith gives the waking words too: alhamdulillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur.

Praise be to Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the rising. The first thought of the day is thanks for being handed back. Around those two lines, the tradition gathers other habits.

Many Muslims make wudu before bed, lie on the right side, and recite the last three short surahs, al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas, blowing lightly into cupped hands and passing them over the body, as Bukhari reports the Prophet did.
Some add the Verse of the Throne.

teach.h: THE LAST THING IS A NAME.
teach.b: None of it takes longer than one more video, and it changes what the last thing is. Not a headline. A name.

how: Many Muslims make wudu before bed, lie on the right side, recite the last three surahs and say 'bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya', and on waking praise Allah for giving life again.

o: a promise to wake early for the morning prayer
words said lying down: in Your name I die and live
a long night prayer prayed after waking at dawn

games.q: what's inside the words before sleep — tap the pairs.
p: in Your name I die and I live
souls taken in sleep, sent back

s: the bedtime words call sleep a kind of dying
in Your name I die and I live, and the Qur'an describes souls taken in sleep (39:42).
the bedtime du'a is long and takes minutes
it's one short line; the wider routine takes less time than one more video.
the Prophet ﷺ is reported to have lain on his right side with his hand under his cheek

games.q: you wake up in the morning. according to the same hadith, what's the first thing the Prophet ﷺ said?
o: praise to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die
a list of the day's plans
games.why: alhamdulillahi alladhi ahyana ba'da ma amatana wa ilayhin-nushur: thanks for being handed back (Bukhari 6324).

practice: Rest one hand under your cheek, or let your head tip slightly to the right, and let the day go one breath at a time: the work, the messages, the argument.
If you pray, say it quietly, bismika Allahumma amutu wa ahya, in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live; if not, simply notice how much you're about to let go of, and let it go.

wordCard.voice: Before sleep. The Prophet's words at bedtime: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live, and on waking, praise for being given life again. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: in Your name, O Allah, I die and I live, the words said on lying down.

carryVoice: Your line: in your name I sleep. And in the morning, you're handed back. Good night, and see you tomorrow.
